chapter: Postwar: Chicago, Vinson, Hines and Cootie
title: Cootie as bandleader; Gator Tail Jackson
summary: Cootie blew every set, drank, and was choosy about drummers; Gus named tenor Willis Jackson 'Gator Tail'.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: That's right, yeah. Was Cootie doing much billing? blowing?
Hm?
Was Cootie doing much billing? blowing?
Oh, yes. He blew all the time, every set.
You enjoyed him, didn't you?
Oh, yes, goodness. He had a good group. Good group.
And he's got such a wonderful concept, with so much power and --
We had a tenor player with us, and I can't think of his name, either. But he didn't work out too well, so we got Gator tail Jackson, from Florida.
Oh, yeah. Yeah. And he blew --
Yes. I've got some records there with that on them. I remember we made.
You enjoyed that.
Oh, sure, yeah. Willis Jackson, he was the -- I gave him the name Gator tail.
Did you?
Because he came from Florida, the alligators there.
Yeah, right.
And I used to tell him all he'd eat was
alligator tail and rice, one of those things.
Yeah.
And we had a very good -- he had a very good band.
And Cootie is very particular about drummers.
Oh, yeah. A good strong man.
And there's a a lot of drummers he doesn't like.
No.
He used to get on Sonny terribly, in the band. He used to -- he didn't like --
Sonny who?
Greer.
Oh, Sonny Greer, yeah.
He used to get very mad.
Well, he had a drummer with his big band. I thought sure he was going to take him, but he didn't.
Who was he? Well, it doesn't matter. I know he's very serious about who he's got playing in back of him.
Yeah, he was -- I'll tell you, he --
But Cootie was drinking, wasn't he?
Oh, he always loved to drink, one of those things.
Because he told me that when he finally got ready to quit the whole thing, he just figured that --
